summary: PASS: no blocking or major finding stands. The three round-2 majors are fixed. (1) T-S65 now schedules the next automatic read at once. (2) T-S58 and T-S59 schedule read 1 as T-S19 does, so no reachable (UnknownOutcome, event) leaves the session with no read scheduled, no Check again and no transition. (3) AGENT-RULES and the bootstrap order now generate v4.1.2, and the bootstrapped code holds CommandEnvelope.Command, RequestContext.Now and ReconcileReadsSentAt. Only ReconcileDue, T-S31 and T-S32 send a reconciliation read; each sends only while fewer than four fall in the 60 s window and records the read. So at most four fall in any 60 s per session. Provenance holds. The package applies exactly what option A lists under 'applies' for ODR-V412-01..03 (APR-V412-OWNER-1) and ODR-V412-05 (APR-V412-OWNER-2), with -05 superseding -01's T-S65. Both records are owner commits and the latest record of each decision. The approvals file has had no agent commit since 2dc5a05. The requests are unchanged since each record; f24b167 changed only the top-level status. v4, v4.1 and v4.1.1 equal their tags. All evidence re-ran green. Three minor findings and three notes remain. T-S65's 'at once, replacing any pending one' has no contract mechanism, and it departs from INV-04's 2/4/8 s spacing unless that read is the 'plus one per offline-to-online change'. The owner's select records are not bound to the content of 'applies'. Some docs are stale.

findings.area: ODR-V412-05: T-S65 'at once, replacing any pending one'
findings.finding: Nothing in the contracts says how an automatic read is replaced, or that a read already in flight is respected. HostEffect.Timer of TimerKey * ms (06-IF41-APP.fs 40-50) has no cancel, and no rule says a timer with the same key replaces the pending one. TimerFired carries no generation, so the engine cannot tell a stale fire from a current one. ReconcileDue (05-IF41-SAVE.fs 215-220) sends 'the next reconciliation read' whenever automatic reads are left, whether or not one is Outstanding. Three cases follow. (a) Read k is in flight, and WentOffline then WentOnline arrive before its answer. T-S65 then makes ReconcileDue send read k+1 at once. Read k's answer becomes SupersededReply (T-S40), so one automatic read is spent with no answer acted on. (b) A host that keeps both timers fires the old T-S29 timer as well. That sends a further read, which supersedes the at-once read. The old timer can even fire in a later UnknownOutcome episode of the same session, and the read it sends comes early. (c) The at-once read can fall well inside INV-04's 'at least 2, 4 and 8 seconds apart'. Example: read 1 at 2 s fails, offline at 2.2 s, online at 2.3 s, read 2 at 2.3 s. Or: AnswerLost at 0 s, offline/online by 0.5 s, read 1 at 0.5 s. INV-04 still holds if each at-once read is counted as the 'plus one per offline-to-online change', but the package never says so, and the INV04.RequestBounds oracle must decide it. Neither case breaks the four-in-60 s bound: every read is still sent by ReconcileDue, T-S31 or T-S32, windowed and recorded. Neither causes a stall either: every case still ends in a resolution or in T-S64 with Check again offered. Stating the timer-replacement semantics and the T-S65 read's place in INV-04's spacing needs contract or transition text, so it needs an owner decision or a clarifying note. Not a blocker.

findings.area: Provenance: the owner's select records are not bound to 'applies' content
findings.finding: Two things are true of an operator select record. It holds only {decision_id, action: select, option}. owner-freeze.fsx 'show' prints the question, rationale, impact, recommendation and options, never 'applies'. ownerRecordsWith compares the package with the 'applies' in the current requests file. So an agent that edits a recorded request's 'applies' and the package the same way passes every check. The mutation that changes T-S65's effects in both ODR-V412-05's 'applies' and the amendments returns NONE from X01-X20 and ownerRecords. Also, owner-freeze 'decide' skips a request already recorded ('not asked again'), so the owner would not be asked again after such an edit. Today this has not happened: I verified every V412 request is identical to its state at the commit of its record (9168153, cce339c). Option A's prose matches 'applies' for all four, and ODR-V412-04's approval will digest the requests file through package-manifest.json. Binding a digest of 'applies' into the record, or having the offline suite compare each request with its blob at the record's commit, would close it.
